problemStatement.plain: Can every sufficiently large integer n be written as n = x^2 + y^2 - z^2 where max(x^2, y^2, z^2) <= n?
whyMatters: Connects representation theory to Fermat-Euler sums of two squares
The strict bound constraint makes the problem substantially harder than unbounded version
